newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says five bids for Telekom sell-off advisor.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says five bids for Telekom sell-off advisor.

text.p: Turkey's Privatisation Administration (OIB) said on Thursday it had received bids from five consortia for the task of advising in the sell-off of state telecommunications company Turk Telekom.
An OIB statement said bids had been put in by the five consortia led by Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, N.M. Rothschild and Salomon Brothers.
Letters will be sent to the bidders inviting them for talks as part of the process of selecting a consortium, the OIB said.
The sale of Turk Telekom is the centrepiece of the Turkish government's privatisation programme, which has received fresh impetus under a four-month-old government eager for badly needed revenues.
A government official told Reuters earlier this week that Turkey expects to raise $3.5 billion from the sale of Telekom.
Officials are aiming to privatise 10-15 percent of the company in the first half of 1997.
Previous attempts to sell off Turk Telekom have been hindered by constitutional challenges, but an amended privatisation law has since been passed.
